::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Linear, first order ODE, given general solution](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/1952192/linear-first-order-ode-given-general-solution), asked by [user118035](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/118035/user118035) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2016-10-03; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> Construct a linear first order ODE of $$xy'+a_0(x)y=g(x)$$
> such that the general solution is $$y=x^3+\frac{c}{x^3}$$
>
> If I substitute the general solution into the question, 
> $$xy'+a_0(x)(x^3+\frac{c}{x^3})=g(x)$$
> this form looks unusual to solve and a(x), g(x) are not given in any expression.  how can I to approach this?
:::

If $y = x^3 + cx^{-3}$ then
$$xy' = x\left(3x^2 -3cx^{-4}\right) = 3x^3 - 3cx^{-3}$$
So
$$xy' + a_0(x) y 
   = 3x^3 - 3cx^{-3}+ a_0(x) \left(x^3 + cx^{-3}\right)
   = (a_0(x)+3)x^3 + c(a_0(x)-3)x^{-3}$$
Since this is to be equal to a function $g(x)$ independent of $c$, we must have $a_0(x)=3$.  It follows that $g(x)=6x^3$ works.
